verdict.rationale: Fellow's own REST API covers a meaningful slice of the UI: listing and reading notes, recordings and transcripts, writing note agendas in a format that round-trips, completing and archiving action items, uploading recordings, plus webhooks and super-admin export and delete. Nothing in the evidence claims API parity with the UI, and many UI capabilities have no documented API surface. Missing for 10: API coverage of recording and bot controls, retention and recording policy settings, keyword tracking, Ask Fellow, workspace and admin settings, action item creation and editing beyond complete/archive, and any vendor statement or independent verification of UI–API parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
Write a note's agenda and/or rename the note. Provide `content_fellow_markdown`, `title`, or both.
The format round-trips: the `content_fellow_markdown` you read from a note is exactly what you can send back to `POST /note/{id}/agenda`.
Mark an action item as complete or incomplete.
Upload a recording from a URL. Use this endpoint to bring an existing meeting recording into Fellow.
Fellow’s Super Admin API lets designated Enterprise‑plan administrators retrieve, export, and delete data across the entire workspace
